events.text: Most people think a side hustle turns into a business the moment somebody pays you.

card.text: Your first sale doesn't make it a business

card.text: Your first sale doesn't make it a business

events.text: Whether you're chasing a profit, or doing something you enjoy that happens to bring in some cash.
And that one question decides a lot.
Whether you can write off your costs.
Whether a bad year lowers the tax on your day job.
Whether you owe pension contributions you didn't plan for.

Now, that cost nobody plans for.
It's insurance.
Most side hustles run out of a home, a car or a garage.
And the home insurance you already pay for usually wasn't written with a business in mind.
The Insurance Bureau of Canada says you must tell your home insurer about a business on your premises.

events.text: And it says most home policies only give a small amount of coverage for books, tools and equipment used for a business.

A customer slips on your step, or your product hurts someone.

Forget the tax rules for a minute.
Is what you have a business, or a second job you made for yourself?
You'd be in good company either way.
